document.abstract: With the Audio Engineering Society's annual conference for 2000 entitled “Surrounded by Sound,” and the SATIS conference in Paris majoring on ‘Surround,‘ it is clear that ‘Surround’ is becoming the “next big thing.” In spite of all the activity, however, the answers to many questions are unclear. What is “surround sound?” How do you record it? How do you play it back? And where is it heading in the market? In this paper I offer some personal answers to these questions.

authors.bio: David Griesinger is a physicist who works in the field of sound and music. He worked through college and graduate school as a recording engineer, where he learned of the tremendous importance of room acoustics in recording technique. After finishing his doctorate in solid state physics (with a nuclear flavour—the Mösbauer effect in Zinc 67) he developed one of the first digital reverberation devices. The product eventually became the Lexicon 224 reverberator. Since then Griesinger has been the principal scientist at Lexicon and is chiefly responsible for the algorithm design that goes into their reverberation and surround sound products. He also has conducted research into the perception and measurement of the acoustical properties of concert halls and opera houses, and is the designer of the LARES reverberation enhancement system.
